title: What Is Cloud Computing?
summary: What the cloud actually is — renting computing over the internet, the IaaS/PaaS/SaaS service models and the shared responsibility that comes with each, public/private/hybrid deployment, the shift from CapEx to OpEx, and the real benefits like elasticity and global reach.

title: What Is Azure and Getting Started
summary: What Microsoft Azure is and how you actually work with it — the account/subscription model, the four main ways to interact (portal, Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell, and Cloud Shell), signing in, and creating your very first resource group.

title: Azure Global Infrastructure
summary: How Azure is laid out across the planet — datacenters grouped into regions, availability zones for in-region resilience, region pairs and geographies for disaster recovery and data residency, and the practical factors that decide which region you pick.

title: Resource Management and ARM
summary: How Azure organizes and manages everything you create — the management-group / subscription / resource-group / resource hierarchy, the Azure Resource Manager control plane that every request goes through, and tags for organizing and tracking cost.

title: Core Compute Overview
summary: A map of Azure's main ways to run code — virtual machines and scale sets (IaaS), App Service (PaaS web hosting), Azure Functions (serverless), and containers (ACI, Container Apps, AKS) — and a simple way to pick the right one for a workload.

title: Core Storage Overview
summary: Azure's core storage building blocks — the storage account and its Blob, File, Queue, and Table services (plus managed disks for VMs), the hot/cool/cold/archive access tiers for blobs, and the LRS/ZRS/GRS/GZRS redundancy options that decide how many copies of your data exist and where.

title: Core Networking Overview
summary: The building blocks of networking in Azure — virtual networks and subnets, network security groups for traffic rules, ways to connect to on-premises (VPN and ExpressRoute), the load-balancing options (Load Balancer, Application Gateway, Front Door, Traffic Manager), and Azure DNS.

title: Identity and Access
summary: How Azure knows who you are and what you may do — Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) as the cloud identity service, authentication versus authorization, Azure role-based access control (RBAC) with scopes and built-in roles, and stronger sign-in with MFA and Conditional Access.

title: Deploy a Virtual Machine
summary: Hands-on with Azure Virtual Machines — creating a Linux VM with the Azure CLI, understanding images, sizes, and managed disks, connecting over SSH, controlling inbound traffic, and (crucially) deallocating and deleting to stop the meter.

title: Host Web Apps with App Service
summary: Deploy a web app or API on Azure App Service — the App Service plan that provides the compute, deploying code with the CLI, scaling up versus out, zero-downtime releases with deployment slots, and adding a custom domain with free managed TLS.

title: Serverless with Azure Functions
summary: Build event-driven serverless code with Azure Functions — how triggers start a function and bindings connect it to data, the hosting plans (Consumption scales to zero but can cold-start; Premium keeps instances warm), what serverless is good and bad at, and creating a function app with the CLI.

title: Store Data with Blob Storage
summary: Work hands-on with Azure Blob storage — containers and blobs, uploading and downloading with the CLI, granting time-limited access with SAS tokens, automating tier changes and cleanup with lifecycle rules, hosting a static website, and preferring Entra ID over account keys.

title: Relational Data with Azure SQL
summary: Run relational databases on Azure — the difference between Azure SQL Database (PaaS), SQL Managed Instance, and SQL Server on a VM, the DTU vs vCore purchasing models (including serverless), configuring the firewall, and connecting to run queries, with backups handled for you.

title: NoSQL with Cosmos DB
summary: Azure Cosmos DB, the globally distributed NoSQL database — its multiple APIs, how throughput is measured and billed in Request Units, why the partition key is the most important design choice, the five consistency levels, and turnkey global distribution.

title: Networking Hands-On
summary: Build a network from the ground up — a virtual network with subnets, a network security group, a VM placed inside it, connecting networks with VNet peering, and reaching PaaS services privately with private endpoints instead of over the public internet.

title: Secrets and Configuration with Key Vault
summary: Keep credentials out of your code — store secrets, keys, and certificates in Azure Key Vault, let apps authenticate with managed identities instead of stored passwords, reference secrets from App Service and Functions, and centralize non-secret settings with App Configuration.

title: Monitoring and Observability
summary: See what your systems are doing — Azure Monitor as the umbrella for metrics and logs, Log Analytics workspaces queried with KQL, Application Insights for application performance, and alerts with action groups that notify or automate a response.

title: Containers on Azure
summary: Run containers on Azure — building and storing images in Azure Container Registry, then choosing where they run: Container Instances for single containers, Container Apps for serverless microservices, or Azure Kubernetes Service for full Kubernetes control.

title: Infrastructure as Code with Bicep
summary: Define your Azure infrastructure in code — why infrastructure as code matters, how ARM templates and the friendlier Bicep language relate, writing and deploying a Bicep file, using parameters for reuse, and previewing changes safely with what-if because deployments are declarative and idempotent.

title: CI/CD to Azure
summary: Automate build, test, and deploy to Azure — what CI/CD means, the two main tools (GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines), authenticating to Azure securely with OIDC/workload identity federation instead of stored secrets, and a workflow that deploys an app on every push.

title: Cost Management and Governance
summary: Keep spending and sprawl under control — estimate with the pricing and TCO calculators, track and forecast real spend with Cost Management and budgets, save with reservations and right-sizing, and enforce the rules with Azure Policy, resource locks, tags, and management groups.

title: Security in Azure
summary: A tour of Azure security — defense in depth and Zero Trust, Microsoft Defender for Cloud with its secure score, Microsoft Sentinel for SIEM/SOAR, encryption at rest and in transit, and the identity and network controls that tie it all together.

title: Reliability and Scaling
summary: Design systems that stay up and keep up — how SLAs and composite SLAs work, availability sets versus availability zones, scaling up versus out with autoscale, and protecting data and continuity with backup and disaster recovery (RTO/RPO).

title: Well-Architected and Capstone
summary: Bring it all together — the five pillars of the Azure Well-Architected Framework and where the Cloud Adoption Framework fits, then a capstone that designs a small, real solution end to end using the compute, storage, data, identity, security, and automation services from this course.
